title: Decision: Two-phase async/sync split in Caller extractor
description: Why this is good: The extractor in FromRequestParts::from_request_parts() splits authorization into two phases: (1) async WhoIs call before acquiring any locks, then (2) synchronous store lookup inside a lock scope. This is necessary because ContactStore holds &Connection which is \!Send (contains RefCell internally). Holding a \!Send reference across .await would make the future \!Send, violating axum's contract. By completing the async work first, then entering a brief lock-protected scope, the future remains Send and the concurrent request handling scales properly. The code comments explain this trade-off explicitly, preventing future maintainers from 'simplifying' it back into a deadlock or Send violation.
